blocks.text: Papallacta: a hot pool in a mountain valley

## Ecuador for travellers who want a more active trip

This route crosses several natural zones, with the altitude and activities changing along the way. Quito sits about 2,800 m above sea level. A cable car then takes the group up to Cruz Loma at 4,000 m, where the trek to the 4,696 m summit of Rucu Pichincha begins.

Next is Cotopaxi National Park, with a horseback ride and a walk by Limpiopungo Lagoon. The route continues to the Quilotoa crater lake and on to the wetter town of Baños, where the canyoning trip includes 3 waterfall descents. At lower elevations, closer to Ecuador’s Amazon region, you’ll raft on the Jatunyacu River. The trip ends at the Papallacta hot springs high in the Andes.
